worlds: W1: target write commits, acknowledgement is lost, then target content and all same-authority historical witnesses are overwritten, rewritten, dereferenced or otherwise unavailable
tested_scope.question: What is the minimal independently surviving witness contract that can distinguish W0 from W1 after the repository/current target no longer disambiguates?
included: same-domain current target/history has collapsed to observational equivalence
ordering of independent witness relative to target commit
excluded: implementation of a new external durability service
claims outside the two-world acknowledgement-loss plus later same-domain-loss model

observations: After all same-authority target/history evidence is lost, W0 and W1 are observationally identical inside that authority domain; any successful discriminator therefore requires surviving outcome information outside the failed domain.

A second durability domain by itself is insufficient. If a client writes an external success witness before the target commit, that witness can exist in W0 when the target commit subsequently fails, creating a false committed inference.

If a client writes the external success witness only after learning the target commit succeeded, W1 can still lack the witness when the target commit succeeds but its acknowledgement is lost before the client can establish the external witness; later same-domain loss then makes W1 indistinguishable from W0.

A read-after-write decision to create the external witness is also insufficient for the adversarial slice when overwrite/history loss can occur before the read yields a durable disambiguating observation.

Information-theoretically the surviving outcome content can be one committed/not-committed bit, but operationally it must be bound to a stable source-qualified effect/attempt identity so concurrent or retried operations cannot misattribute the bit.

The exact sufficient contract for this slice is therefore an independently durable, source-qualified commit-outcome certificate with causal/atomic coupling: successful target commit implies durable success-certificate existence, while failed target commit cannot produce that success certificate. Equivalent implementations may use atomic cross-domain commit, a fenced target-side hook, or authority-generated receipt, but the coupling semantics—not merely a second store—are the essential mechanism.

minimality_result.necessary_outcome_information: at least one surviving bit distinguishing committed from not-committed outside the failed same-authority domain
minimality_result.necessary_coupling: target-commit success causally/atomically entails success-certificate durability; failed target commit cannot entail the same success certificate
insufficient_variants: independent witness written only before target commit
independent witness written only after client observes target success

o_comparison.reason: Existing role-local evidence established same-domain journals/CAS/idempotency and partial durability mechanisms plus no currently authorized independent zero-cost/no-finite-quota closure surface. This bounded leaf does not claim global absence from O; it establishes that the exact coupled independent commit-outcome certificate required by this failure model has not been demonstrated as an authorized Phase-1 mechanism.

phase1_gates.reason_acceptance_withheld: No already-authorized mechanism has been established that supplies the required independent source-qualified commit-outcome certificate with the necessary commit coupling under all tested failure timings.

conclusion: A second durability domain alone does not close the acknowledgement-loss plus later same-domain-loss ambiguity. For the tested scope, the minimal full discriminator is an independently durable, source-qualified commit-outcome certificate causally/atomically coupled to target commit success. No authorized zero-Work, zero-finite-quota, zero-cost realization is established, so Phase 1 remains open.
uncertainty: This is a mechanism-level necessity/sufficiency result for the stated two-world model, not a proof about all storage, distributed-commit or Git failure models.
Equivalent coupling may be implemented by mechanisms not enumerated here; exact identity and causal guarantees, not product names, determine equivalence.
No claim is made that O globally lacks every possible implementation; only that current authorized Phase-1 evidence does not establish this exact contract.

continuation.exact_next_action: On the next invocation after a fresh authoritative bootstrap, test exactly whether any already-authorized zero-cost, zero-finite-quota, non-Work surface can provide target-commit-implies-durable-source-qualified-success-certificate and failed-target-commit-implies-no-success-certificate semantics without sharing the O/repository rewind authority. Do not implement a new service, mutate protected O, or begin any second optional leaf in the current invocation.
